user.title: Connect your Cync account
user.description: Cync LAN controls your devices entirely on your local network at runtime. Your account credentials are only used once, here, to pull down your device list - they are not stored in plain text and are not used again unless you re-run setup.

otp.title: Enter the verification code
otp.description: Cync emailed a one-time verification code to your account email address.

confirm.title: Confirm setup
confirm.description: Found {device_count} device(s) on your Cync account. Continue to finish setup and start the local listener.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate with Cync
reauth_confirm.description: Cync LAN needs to sign in to your account again - the cached session expired or your password changed.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the Cync cloud API. Check your internet connection and try again.
error.no_devices: No devices were found on this Cync account.

abort.already_configured: This Cync account is already configured. Only one Cync LAN account is supported per Home Assistant instance.

motion_sensor_select.title: Edit motion sensor settings
motion_sensor_select.description: Choose which motion or ambient-light sensor to edit.

motion_sensor_wake.title: Wake up {device_name}
motion_sensor_wake.description:
{device_name} appears to be offline right now. Press and hold its off button for 5 seconds to wake the device & make it discoverable. The LED light will turn green.

Make sure your phone/hub is within 40 feet of the device during this process, then select Submit to check again.

motion_sensor_settings.title: Motion sensor settings for {device_name}
motion_sensor_settings.description: {device_name} is online. Choose which sensor to tune and its new settings - this sends the change immediately.

error.still_offline: Still offline - hold the off button for 5 seconds until the LED turns green, then try again.

abort.no_motion_sensors: No motion or ambient-light sensors were found on this Cync LAN account, or the integration hasn't finished starting yet.

no_devices_connected.title: No Cync devices have connected
no_devices_connected.description: No Cync devices have connected to the local listener on port {port} since setup finished. This almost always means the DNS redirection prerequisite isn't actually in place yet, or the affected devices haven't been power-cycled since you set it up (they only do a fresh DNS lookup on boot). See the integration's README for the DNS redirection steps, then power-cycle your devices.

experimental_set_indicator_led.name: Set indicator LED (experimental)
experimental_set_indicator_led.description: Confirmed working on real hardware (see docs/mesh_opcodes.md). Kept under the experimental_ service name since it's still a recently-corrected command. Sets a device's small status/indicator LED mode, color, and brightness.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The Cync device whose indicator LED to set.

mode.name: Mode
mode.description: Always on, always off, or normal operation.

color.name: Color
color.description: The indicator LED only supports these 4 colors, not full RGB.

wifi_disconnect_blink.name: Blink on WiFi disconnect
wifi_disconnect_blink.description: Blink the indicator LED when the device loses its WiFi connection.

experimental_set_motion_sensor_settings.name: Set motion/ambient sensor settings (experimental)
experimental_set_motion_sensor_settings.description: Experimental — the outer command byte is predicted, not confirmed against a real packet capture. Tunes a motion or ambient-light sensor's enabled state, sensitivity, and timing. Please report success or failure with your device model, see docs/mesh_opcodes.md. Note: the real Cync app requires physically waking the sensor first (press and hold its off button for 5 seconds - the LED turns green when it's discoverable, and your phone should be within 40 feet) before it accepts settings edits. This isn't a special radio mode - it's the device's ordinary online status, confirmed via decompiled-source research. If this call appears to silently do nothing, the sensor is very likely still asleep - the real app itself silently no-ops this exact command family when its target is offline, rather than erroring.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The Cync device with the sensor to tune.

sensor_type.name: Sensor type
sensor_type.description: Which sensor on the device to tune.

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.description: Turn the sensor on or off. Leave unset to update sensitivity/timing without changing the enabled state.

sensitivity.name: Sensitivity
sensitivity.description: Only applies when updating sensitivity/timing (enabled left unset).

delay_seconds.name: Delay
delay_seconds.description: Only applies when updating sensitivity/timing (enabled left unset).

deactivation_seconds.name: Deactivation delay
deactivation_seconds.description: Only applies when updating sensitivity/timing (enabled left unset).

experimental_execute_scene.name: Activate a Cync scene (experimental)
experimental_execute_scene.description: Experimental — both the outer command byte and the target address are predicted, not confirmed against a real packet capture. Activates a saved Cync Scene (a named multi-device state snapshot configured in the Cync app). Please report success or failure with your device model, see docs/mesh_opcodes.md.

device_id.name: Bridge device
device_id.description: Scenes are home-wide, not per-device - select the "Cync LAN Bridge" device, not an individual light/switch.

scene_id.name: Scene ID
scene_id.description: The numeric ID of the scene to activate, as configured in the Cync app (0-255).

experimental_set_group_power.name: Set a group's power (experimental)
experimental_set_group_power.description: Experimental — unlike this integration's other experimental services, the command itself (set_power) is fully confirmed; what's unconfirmed is whether device firmware actually responds to a group address as "the whole group" rather than a single device. Please report success or failure with your device model, see docs/mesh_opcodes.md.

device_id.name: Bridge device
device_id.description: Groups are addressed home-wide via the group's own mesh address, not per-device - select the "Cync LAN Bridge" device, not an individual light/switch.

group_id.name: Group ID
group_id.description: The group's numeric mesh address (32768-65535) - find it in your exported cync_mesh.yaml/raw_mesh.cync, not a value the Cync app displays directly.

state.name: State
state.description: On or off for every device in the group.

experimental_set_motion_sensor_schedule.name: Set a motion sensor schedule slot (experimental)
experimental_set_motion_sensor_schedule.description: Experimental — the outer command byte is confirmed (same fix already confirmed working on real hardware for the indicator LED service), but the predicted cmd_code and this specific command have not themselves been tested against real hardware. Writes one of a group's 4 fixed motion-sensor schedule slots. Please report success or failure with your device model, see docs/mesh_opcodes.md. Note: the real Cync app requires physically waking the sensor first (press and hold its off button for 5 seconds - the LED turns green when it's discoverable, and your phone should be within 40 feet) before it accepts settings edits. This isn't a special radio mode - it's the device's ordinary online status, confirmed via decompiled-source research. If this call appears to silently do nothing, the sensor is very likely still asleep - the real app itself silently no-ops this exact command family when its target is offline, rather than erroring.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The motion/ambient-light sensor device to write the schedule to.

slot.name: Slot
slot.description: Which of the 4 fixed time-of-day slots to write.

mode.name: Mode
mode.description: Disabled, occupancy-based, vacancy-based, or simple (time-based only).

cct.name: Color temperature
cct.description: 0 (warmest) to 100 (coolest). Exactly one of Color temperature or RGB color must be set.

rgb.name: RGB color
rgb.description: Exactly one of Color temperature or RGB color must be set.

experimental_delete_scene.name: Delete a Cync scene (experimental)
experimental_delete_scene.description: Experimental — the outer command byte is directly confirmed (DeleteSceneHubCommand's own op_code, not the hardcoded-0x8E relay bug), but whether this command's real wire frame even rides over the same connection cync-lan intercepts at all is unconfirmed - the app builds it via a structurally different, separately-flagged-deprecated framer. Sent through cync-lan's own confirmed envelope as an experiment. Please report success or failure with your device model, see docs/cync_automations.md.

device_id.name: Bridge device
device_id.description: Scenes are home-wide, not per-device - select the "Cync LAN Bridge" device, not an individual light/switch.

scene_id.name: Scene ID
scene_id.description: The numeric ID of the scene to delete, as configured in the Cync app (0-65535).

experimental_delete_schedule.name: Delete a Cync schedule (experimental)
experimental_delete_schedule.description: Experimental — same situation as the delete-scene service: the outer command byte is directly confirmed, but whether this command's real wire frame rides over the same connection cync-lan intercepts at all is unconfirmed. Sent through cync-lan's own confirmed envelope as an experiment. Please report success or failure with your device model, see docs/cync_automations.md.

device_id.name: Bridge device
device_id.description: Schedules are home-wide, not per-device - select the "Cync LAN Bridge" device, not an individual light/switch.

schedule_id.name: Schedule ID
schedule_id.description: The numeric ID of the schedule to delete, as configured in the Cync app (0-65535).

experimental_toggle_automation.name: Enable or disable a Cync schedule (experimental)
experimental_toggle_automation.description: Experimental — same situation as the delete-scene/delete-schedule services: the outer command byte is directly confirmed, but whether this command's real wire frame rides over the same connection cync-lan intercepts at all is unconfirmed. Sent through cync-lan's own confirmed envelope as an experiment. Enables or disables a saved Schedule without deleting it. Please report success or failure with your device model, see docs/cync_automations.md.

device_id.name: Bridge device
device_id.description: Schedules are home-wide, not per-device - select the "Cync LAN Bridge" device, not an individual light/switch.

schedule_id.name: Schedule ID
schedule_id.description: The numeric ID of the schedule to toggle, as configured in the Cync app (0-65535).

scene_id.name: Scene ID
scene_id.description: The scene this schedule triggers - the app writes this same field with a different byte width than the delete-scene service, per real app-code inconsistency (0-4294967295).

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.description: Whether the schedule should be active.
